title: The fixed-point format is never used together with reaction names
reviewer_why: Line 37's '& 0' deliberately disables the fixed-point branch; the header documents no print format, so the exponential output contradicts no documentation or result. At most a style or cleanup note, and it does not quarantine either way.

title: The size plot is never produced without a stratification file
reviewer_why: The behaviour is real: '~numel(...)==1' at line 108 parses as (~numel)==1, which is false for nonempty data, so lines 109-117 never run. But no option is involved: the plot is the default behaviour for nargin<6, and code that is never reached falls under wrong-result (evident intent, comment at line 107), not unusable-option. It still quarantines.

title: The sheets written with xlswrite need Microsoft Excel
reviewer_why: Lines 98-103, 116-117, 133-134 and 199 use xlswrite, which without Excel falls back to CSV (numeric only); the documented options RankingGeneID and differ_genes therefore misplace output or fail (SUMMARY, line 199) on every non-Windows platform, and the header states no Excel requirement, so by the rule a documented option fails when used (same platform reasoning as ACHRSamplerParallelGeneral's Linux defect). Does not change the quarantine.

title: The fallback to the reversed reaction <name>_r never runs
reviewer_why: findRxnIDs returns 0 (ismember) for an absent name, so isempty at lines 40 and 55 is never true and line 46 indexes with 0. For a model that holds only <name>_r (an irreversible-split model), the call with <name> is the case lines 41 and 56-57 are written for; handling code that is never reached on that input is wrong-result by the rule. The given trigger ('r1_' with no 'r1__r') does not exercise that case. Does not change the quarantine.

title: The output file is named gc_data_webGCM.txt, not gc_data_webCGM.txt as documented
reviewer_why: Line 44 writes gc_data_webGCM.txt while OUTPUT (line 25) says gc_data_webCGM.txt; the data are written, and other code (dGfzeroGroupContToBiochemical.m line 104) refers to gc_data_webGCM.txt, so the documentation is what misnames the file. Does not change the quarantine.

title: The optional input modelMetaData cannot be omitted
reviewer_why: modelMetaData is listed under OPTIONAL INPUTS (line 18) but line 43 uses it without a default, so any call omitting it errors; omitting a documented optional input is a documented call that fails, i.e. error, not limitation.

title: a row with rational coefficients is lost
reviewer_why: The '/' branch (lines 123-136) never stores the row, which therefore becomes an all-zero ray; line 157 removes it and line 159 indexes R with a sort permutation of the original length, so any rational row ends in an index error rather than a wrong value - a documented lrs input (rationals) that fails.

title: vartype is dropped from the default output
reviewer_why: Real: line 206 (default writeMatrix=true, default solverParams) calls BuildMPS without the 'Integer'/'Binary' lists built at 186-187. But the writeMatrix help (lines 32-33) documents that the default writes 'only the Matrix, not the full problem', and writeMatrix=false (line 209) does pass vartype, so the caller gets what writeMatrix documents; only the .vartype text is imprecise.

title: A model without any gene rule stops with an error
reviewer_why: An all-empty grRules leaves term2 (and term) undefined at line 115. The doc allows any n x 1 grRules cell and nothing forbids all-empty, so by the rule this is a documented input that fails. It does not change the quarantine.

title: A SEED identifier given as a cell stops the function
reviewer_why: A nested-cell SEED id is not a documented or produced format: verifyModelBorg builds metSEEDID as a cell of char (its line 272), and nothing defines cell-valued entries. The iscell handling at lines 145-147 covers KEGG only, so the SEED failure is an undocumented input.

title: rules and rxnGeneMat are never built
reviewer_why: rxnGeneMat is created all-zero at line 216 and line 219 tests its sum, so lines 220-242 (rules/rxnGeneMat construction, with the comment 'only make the rules if there are grRules') can never run. That is handling code never reached on a valid input, which the rule classes as wrong-result, not limitation. It does not change the quarantine.

title: metabolite and uptake/secretion features are looked up in the reaction database
reviewer_why: This changes the written table: Description/Formula/Subsystem stay empty for every metabolite-presence and uptake/secretion feature (i=2,3 go through the reaction lookup at lines 51-56). The i==4 branch (line 69) shows that metabolite features are meant to be looked up in database.metabolites. It is not a documentation-only problem; mild, and it does not change the quarantine.

title: The missing-formula warning tests the whole formula list
reviewer_why: Line 108 strcmp(model.metFormulas,'') is a vector, so with some (not all) empty formulas line 115 calls numAtomsOfElementInFormula('', 'H'), which indexes formula(1) at its line 38 and errors; the unreached handling at lines 109-113 shows partial missing formulas are an intended input, so the caller gets an error, not just a missing warning.

title: A flux vector of zeros gives NaN widths
reviewer_why: An all-zero fbaSolution.v is a valid documented input (n x 1 flux vector); line 62 divides by max = 0, giving NaN widths, while lines 70 and 82 show the intent that non-carrying reactions get width 1. Not an undocumented input, so not a limitation.

title: A flux of exactly 1e-3 of the largest flux keeps width 0.001
reviewer_why: Lines 69-70 use > 1e-3 and < 1e-3, so a ratio of exactly 1e-3 keeps the raw ratio as its width; the caller receives a width outside the band set, which changes the result, not just documentation (minor boundary case).

title: (new entry)
action: add a wrong-result entry: the local objective pdcoObj (line 74) returns alpha*x'*(log(x)-x) = alpha*sum(x.*log(x) - x.^2), while its gradient (line 75) alpha*log(x) and Hessian (line 76) belong to alpha*sum(x.*log(x) - x); objective and derivatives disagree. Keep the existing entries.
